evaluator_settings.rationale: A 0.2 MHz grid resolves assignment margins and notch crossings without hiding the chosen numerical resolution.
The representative isolated-slot feedline length is explicit and separate from resonator-line matrices.
The loaded-bare scan spans both expected modes and their probe-induced motion.
Ownership is limited to the independently expected slot neighborhood.

A 1 MHz margin is five 0.2 MHz samples and prevents a numerical tie from becoming physical ownership.
The isolated-pair trace contains both hybridized poles and background evidence.
The complex fit is restricted to the coupled-pair neighborhood.
Background samples begin outside the 180 MHz fit window.
The intrinsic Z21 scan brackets the 4.5 GHz notch target.
Four distinct finite probes support a free-intercept frequency extrapolation and a zero-constrained even linewidth fit while retaining two-pole visibility.
Frequency extrapolation must be nearly quadratic before its zero-probe intercept is consumed.
The LC-only Maxwell-diagonal reference has no readout decay path at zero probe, so its C^2+C^4 zero-constrained linewidth fit receives an independent quality gate without clamping.
The sampled PTC imaginary transfer impedance must be close to a true zero crossing.
Positive ordered bounds cover the physically intended coupling range.
Separated starts test basin stability around weak, proposed, and strong coupling.
The explicit linear solve cutoff avoids platform-dependent implicit rank decisions.
The nonlinear fit budget is finite and reviewable.
Tight cost convergence supports precision fitting.
Tight parameter convergence supports precision fitting.
Tight gradient convergence supports precision fitting.
The finite-difference perturbation is explicit for replay.
Every declared J start must converge successfully.
At least 80 percent of starts must succeed; the count gate is stricter for this three-seed grid.
Near-optimal support includes starts within five percent of the winning MSE.
An absolute floor keeps the near-optimal test defined when the best MSE is tiny.
At least two distinct starts must support the winning basin.
Filter-only channel calibration uses a narrower central fit window.
Calibration background begins outside its central fit window.
The fixed complex residue is consumed only after a strong complex-data fit.
Amplitude agreement independently guards the channel calibration.
Phase residuals constrain calibration beyond magnitude-only agreement.
Reference division is allowed only away from a through-reference null.

Pair-fit phase error must remain small.
Accepted J fits must remain at least two percent inside parameter bounds.
Near-optimal multistart J estimates must agree within 0.2 MHz.
Two scalar background poles provide an independent local rational cross-check.
Low-Q rational poles are excluded from resonant mode evidence.
The independent vector model must reproduce normalized complex S21.
Independent vector and physical-model poles must agree within 1 MHz.
The independent pole-pair center must preserve the loaded-bare reference center.
